correctness.rationale: For a branch write y=x+s x(1−x), |s|≤1. The image of an interior point stays interior, including s=±1. Expansion gives x(1−x)f′(x)=y(1−y)+(y−x)². Thus the log-odds branch derivative is exactly 1+(y−x)²/[y(1−y)]. Staying off both thresholds ensures a smooth branch itinerary locally through each finite return. Over the cycle the log-odds coordinate factors cancel, and at least one step is nonzero. The product is therefore >1 and is bounded below by 1+4 times the sum of the squared increments, using y(1−y)≤1/4 and dropping all cross terms. This proves hyperbolic repulsion at every least period in scope. Independently, the specified example has steps ±7/50, ordinary derivatives 61/40 and 449/561, product 27389/22440, and lower bound 723/625. CHECK.py was inspected, not executed; the exact arithmetic and branch proof do not depend on that script. No differentiability at the cuts or conclusion about their periodic cycles or about endpoints is needed.

value.rationale: A parameter- and period-uniform stability obstruction resolves a natural question about the existing two-cut model: existence results for specific cycles cannot determine whether an interior, smooth itinerant attractor can be periodic. The formula gives a quantitative reason that holds even on branches with ordinary contraction, and the rational two-cycle establishes that the obstruction is not vacuous. Neither global convergence nor exclusion of border cycles is claimed.
